content.value_statement: Weak subject lines waste test traffic and hide truncation or spam risks. This skill creates and pre-scores subject and preheader variants before campaign testing.
actual_capabilities: Generates three to eight labeled subject line variants.
Creates matched preheaders that extend each subject line.
Checks subject and preheader length for desktop and mobile truncation.
Flags heuristic spam triggers, deceptive prefixes, and symbol stacking.
Counts emoji use and applies stricter cold-outbound guidance.
Ranks variants and explains which candidates should advance or be cut.
limitations: Does not guarantee inbox placement or provider spam scoring.
Does not write email body copy or campaign CTAs.
Does not design A/B tests or calculate statistical significance.
Needs user-provided claims, offers, or source data for factual hooks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Promotional Campaign Tests
use_cases.description: Create subject and preheader options, then rank them before an email marketing test.

use_cases.title: Screen Cold-Outbound Subjects
use_cases.description: Check candidate subject lines for emoji use, deceptive prefixes, and trust risks.

use_cases.title: Improve Newsletter Opens
use_cases.description: Compare newsletter subject angles and preview text before scheduling a send.

prompt_templates.title: Score Existing Subjects
prompt_templates.prompt: Pre-score these subject lines and preheaders for mobile truncation, spam triggers, emoji use, and inbox preview quality: [paste candidates].

prompt_templates.title: Generate Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a starter set from one offer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate five subject line and preheader variants for this offer: [offer]. Use promo mode and rank the strongest options.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Campaign Angles
prompt_templates.prompt: Create subject and preheader variants across curiosity, benefit, offer, personalization, and question angles for [campaign]. Explain which ones should advance.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Test Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff to an experiment designer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a ranked subject line shortlist for [campaign], include pre-score flags, preserve stable variant IDs, and write a concise test handoff summary.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for subject lines for a limited-time product bundle.
output: A table of labeled subject and preheader variants.
Per-variant notes for truncation, spam triggers, emoji use, and preview quality.
A ranked shortlist naming which variants advance and which are cut.

output_examples.input: A sales team pastes cold-outbound subject candidates.
output: A pre-score card for each candidate.
Flags for deceptive prefixes, unsupported claims, emoji use, and broken personalization tokens.
Suggested edits that keep the original sales angle intact.

output_examples.input: A newsletter editor wants to compare curiosity and benefit angles.
output: A recommendation for the strongest test-ready subject set.

best_practices: Provide the campaign mode, offer, from-name, and any required factual claims.
Use the ranked shortlist as preparation for a controlled test, not as a final verdict.
Keep preheaders additive so they expand the subject instead of repeating it.
anti_patterns: Do not use fabricated scarcity, discounts, prices, or performance claims.
Do not treat a clean heuristic score as an inbox placement guarantee.
Do not silently remove weak variants without explaining the reason.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee better open rates?
faq.answer: No. It prepares stronger candidates for testing, but real performance needs campaign data.

faq.question: Can it check full email deliverability?
faq.answer: No. It only flags subject and preheader patterns before a full deliverability review.

faq.question: Can it write the email body?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on subject lines, preheaders, preview rendering, and test handoff notes.

faq.question: What inputs improve the output?
faq.answer: Provide the offer, audience, campaign mode, from-name, preheader goal, and any past subject performance data.

faq.question: Does it support cold outbound?
faq.answer: Yes. It applies stricter trust and emoji guidance for B2B cold-outbound subjects.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.
